currentContext.business: Mac Charles (India) Limited is engaged in the ownership and management of commercial real estate assets, wind energy generation, and real estate development activities. The Company has historically operated as a hospitality and commercial real estate asset owner and has expanded its objects clause to include real estate development in line with its long-term value creation strategy. Its flagship commercial asset is Embassy Zenith in Bengaluru, a fully leased Grade A office building licensed to a single organisation under a leave and license arrangement, while its wind turbine generators supply electricity for captive consumption and for sale to GESCOM, HESCOM and third-party consumers. Customers are business-to-business and operations are confined to Karnataka.

Office rentals (commercial real estate): Embassy Zenith, Bengaluru (Grade A CBD office building)
Sale of electricity (wind energy): Wind turbine generators (WTGs) supplying GESCOM, HESCOM, group captive and third-party consumers
Real estate development: Real estate and property development business added via the amended Main Objects Clause; no named project disclosed

currentContext.strengths: Flagship asset Embassy Zenith is a fully leased Grade A office building in Bengaluru's Central Business District, described as a significant long-term strategic holding.|Positioned in India's largest office market by net absorption - Bengaluru accounted for 26% of total national office leasing in CY 2025, with vacancy declining to 12.0% and average rentals up 9% year-on-year.|Zenith was purpose-built on the erstwhile Le Meridien hotel site to capitalise on demand for Grade A office space in the Bangalore CBD, and is licensed to a reputed organisation under a leave and license arrangement.|Owned wind turbine generators in Gadag and Bellary districts provide a self-generated renewable electricity stream sold under existing power purchase arrangements to GESCOM, HESCOM and group captive consumers.|Existing land and asset base provides optionality for development of premium residential and mixed-use projects.|Part of the Embassy group - Embassy Property Developments Private Limited is the holding company - with four wholly owned real estate subsidiaries.
currentContext.strategies: Optimise returns from existing assets, selectively expand the development pipeline and improve capital efficiency - the stated medium-term strategy.|Extend beyond commercial asset ownership into real estate development, having expanded the Company's objects to include development activities in line with its long-term value creation strategy.|Target the premium residential segment for any new project launches, consistent with Bengaluru's prevailing demand profile.|Evaluate development opportunities across the existing land and asset base, including addition of new development projects.|Treat the finance cost burden as a priority area for management attention, with any material progress on debt restructuring or refinancing to be disclosed as required.|Continue electricity generation and sales to GESCOM, HESCOM and group captive consumers under existing power purchase arrangements.|No dividend, payout or reinvestment policy is set out in the routed governance sections. The Corporate Governance Report states only a general intent: the Company is focused on the enhancement of long-term value creation for all stakeholders without compromising on integrity, social obligations, environment and regulatory compliances, and is committed to focusing its energies and resources on creating and positively leveraging shareholders' wealth while safeguarding the interest of all stakeholders. On related-party dealings the Company confirms all transactions were at arm's length and in the ordinary course of business, with no materially significant related party transactions with promoters, directors or KMP that could conflict with the Company's interest, and a Board-approved Policy on Related Party Transactions in place.|No ESG targets are set: BRSR Section B records 'N.A.' against all nine NGRBC principles for 'Specific commitments, goals and targets set by the entity with defined timelines' and for performance against them.|Renewable generation is the Company's principal environmental contribution - during the year under review it generated about 1,83,07,394 units of green power from its wind turbine generators, supplied to GESCOM, HESCOM and others.|Board-level ESG oversight: the Board of Directors is the highest authority responsible for implementation and oversight of the business responsibility policies, and a Risk Management Committee and CSR Committee oversee community, social and sustainability activities with specific emphasis on ESG issues, with the Whole Time Director and CFO also involved.|Policies cover each of the nine NGRBC principles and have been translated into procedures, but they do NOT extend to value chain partners for any of the nine principles.|No national or international codes, certifications, labels or standards (e.g. SA 8000, OHSAS, ISO, BIS) have been adopted and mapped to the principles - reported as 'N.A.' for all nine principles.|No external assurance and no independent evaluation: the BRSR names no assurance provider and no type of assurance obtained, and the entity has not carried out any independent assessment of its policies by an external agency, relying on internal audits and reviews only.|The BRSR reporting boundary is standalone only, so the four wholly owned subsidiaries are outside the reported ESG data even though they are stated to participate in the Company's business responsibility initiatives.|No material responsible business conduct or sustainability issues have been identified - the BRSR 'material issues' table (risk/opportunity, rationale, mitigation, financial implications) is filled 'N.A.'.|CSR under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 is not applicable to the Company.|Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for all stakeholder groups (communities, investors, shareholders, employees, customers and value chain partners), with the policy published on the Company's investor relations page.|Reviews of performance against the policies and of statutory compliance are undertaken periodically by department heads, business heads and executive directors, with a half-yearly statutory compliance certificate provided by the CFO to the Board.
currentContext.expansion: The Company's principal expansion event of the year was the completion of its landmark commercial building, Zenith, constructed on the erstwhile site of the Le Meridien hotel in the Central Business District of Bangalore. The development was undertaken to capitalise on the strong demand for Grade A office space in the Bangalore CBD; it has been licensed to a reputed organisation under a leave and license arrangement and generated rental income during the year under review, and is expected to deliver improved returns on capital employed. The build-out follows the Company's diversification into the real estate and property development business pursuant to the amended Main Objects Clause of the Memorandum of Association approved by shareholders. No new named capex project, capital outlay, capacity addition or commissioning timeline is disclosed - the Company states only that it continues to evaluate opportunities for development of its existing real estate assets and addition of new development projects in line with its strategic priorities. On the energy side the Company operates wind turbine generators for captive consumption and sale of electricity to GESCOM, HESCOM and third-party consumers, with no capacity addition announced. In the group structure, wholly owned subsidiary Mac Charles Hub Projects Private Limited became a debt-listed entity during the year upon listing of its debt securities on BSE Limited.
currentContext.mdna: Embassy Zenith remains fully leased; continued rental growth in the Bengaluru CBD/off-CBD office market and sustained GCC demand are expected to support stable and growing rental income over the medium term.|Bengaluru's sustained GCC-led office demand, declining vacancy rates and 9% YoY rental growth create a favourable backdrop for rental income appreciation and asset value enhancement at Embassy Zenith.|Bengaluru retained its position as India's largest office market by net absorption, accounting for 26% of total national office leasing in CY 2025, with vacancy declining to 12.0% from 12.3%.|Premiumisation of the Bengaluru residential market - the Rs 1.5 crore to Rs 2.5 crore segment accounted for 45% of new supply in 2025 versus 24% in 2024 - underpins the Company's premium residential positioning.|The Company's existing land and asset base provides optionality for development of premium residential and mixed-use projects.|Evolving SEBI regulations around Small and Medium REITs (SM REITs) and fractional ownership platforms are expanding the investor base for commercial real estate assets, potentially unlocking monetisation opportunities.|Adoption of building management technology, energy efficiency improvements and smart infrastructure investments are expected to improve operational performance and occupier experience at commercial assets.|Increasing state-level demand for renewable power supports sustained electricity generation and sales to GESCOM, HESCOM and group captive consumers.|Notwithstanding near-term macro uncertainties, the structural demand environment for commercial real estate in Bengaluru and the broader Indian real estate sector remains supportive.|No order book is disclosed. The development pipeline is described only qualitatively - the Company is evaluating development opportunities across its existing asset base, with no named project, size or launch date given.

risks.note: The Company's commercial revenue is substantially dependent on a single asset - Embassy Zenith. Any material deterioration in occupancy, tenant credit quality or rental reversion at this asset could have a disproportionate impact on financial performance.

risks.risk: Geographic and single-market concentration in Bengaluru / Karnataka
risks.note: The revenue base is concentrated in Bengaluru, making it sensitive to local market conditions. BRSR discloses operations in a single state (Karnataka), exports of NIL as a percentage of turnover, and business-to-business customers only, with plants limited to wind turbine generators in Gadag and Bellary districts and the Zenith building at Sankey.

The real estate sector operates under a multi-layered regulatory framework spanning central, state and local authorities. Delays in project clearances or changes in land use regulations can impact development timelines and project viability, and RERA compliance requirements continue to evolve across states.

risks.risk: General economic conditions, interest rates and liquidity
risks.note: A slowdown in India's economic growth, rising interest rates or tightening liquidity conditions could dampen commercial office demand, reduce new leasing activity and affect home buyer affordability.

Development activity is exposed to volatility in construction material prices (particularly steel and cement), labour availability and logistics costs. Cost overruns can compress project margins, particularly for mid-scale developers with limited procurement leverage.

risks.risk: Energy market risk in the windmill segment
risks.note: The windmill segment is subject to variability in wind resource availability and to DISCOM-related exposure; the Company's electricity offtake is concentrated in GESCOM and HESCOM. (The routed text is truncated mid-sentence, so the full description of this risk is not available.)

risks.risk: Sector-level land availability and regulatory complexity
risks.note: Limited land in prime urban locations increases project costs, while complex acquisition processes and JDA structures add execution risk; multiple clearance requirements and inconsistent state-level implementation of regulations continue to delay project timelines.
